answer: Whether an agent catalogs a relic, audits a vault, or maps karst, it must lock 100 tokens in escrow for 90 days before its identity gets one vote in the market’s governance. Creating more names creates no free votes: controlling 1,000 voting identities requires locking 100,000 tokens. The bond makes a sybil swarm costly through capital requirements and foregone use of those funds, though a wealthy attacker can still buy influence.
